listOfChildMeasurements.name: Length Uncertainty

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Major (normally longer) dimension of an object; the actual type of measurement depends upon the shape of the object. [Used for Drilling Targets, whose shapes could be Elliptical, Circular, Rectangular...]
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Major Dimension

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Liquid radius in the Bowl = Bowl Inner Radius - Pond_Depth
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Centrifuge Liquid Radius

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Distance from the Measure Point to the Reference Plane for the assembly or tool; a positive value indicates that the Measure Point is above the Reference Plane.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Measure Point Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The distance from the bottom of the Equipment to the point where the pressure is measured.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Pressure Measure Point

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The distance from the bottom of the Equipment to the point where the Temperature is measured
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Temperature Measure Point

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Distance from the Measure Point to the Tool Reference Plane (most often the bottom tool make-up plane); a positive value indicates that the Measure Point is above the Reference Plane. [Traditionally stored in Parameter MPOI on LIS/DLIS tapes.]
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Tool Measure Point Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Distance from the Measure Point to the Tool String (not just Tool!) Reference Plane; a positive value indicates that the Measure Point is above the Reference Plane. [Traditionally referred to as "tool zero".]
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Tool String Measure Point Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Distance from the Measure Reference Plane to the bottom of the Equipment (which is for a tool practically the make-up line of the bottom connection). The Measure Reference Plane allows recording of the location of the sensor measure point in an equipment composition. The measure point is positioned by a length called Measure_Point_Offset, a property of the composition to which the sensor belongs. The Measure_Point_Offset is the distance from the measure reference plane of the part, i.e., sensor or tool, to the measure reference plane of the whole, i.e., tool or tool string.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Measure Reference Plane Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Minor (normally shorter) dimension of an object; the actual type of measurement depends upon the shape of the object. [Used for Drilling Targets, whose shapes could be Elliptical, Circular, Rectangular...]
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Minor Dimension

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average straight-line distance a neutron travels at thermal energy levels before being absorbed by a formation nucleus.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Neutron Diffusion Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average straight-line distance a neutron travels in being slowed from natural source energy to epithermal energy levels by collisions with formation nuclei.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Neutron Slowing Down Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: For non-equidistant receiver groups, distance to next group
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Distance to Next Receiver Group

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Nominal (approximate, for naming purposes only) length of an equipment item.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Nominal Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Nominal length of tube of body of equipment item.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Tube Nominal Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Nominal distance between consecutive receiver groups
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Nominal Receiver Group Distance

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Nominal distance between stations on a seismic line
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Nominal Station Distance

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of the portion of the perforation which extends from the casing beyond the cement sheath and into the reservoir. It includes the casing thickness and the cement sheath thickness.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Perforation Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Total penetration in an API Section I test
listOfChildMeasurements.name: API Total Penetration

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of the portion of the perforation which is filled with Gravel Pack material.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gravel Pack Perforation Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Measure of slope using the linear distance between two successive points: on a screw, between threads, measured parallel to the axis; for a propeller or spinner, the theoretical axial displacement corresponding to one revolution.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Pitch

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The nominal length of the streamer.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Streamer Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Half Length of the part of an hydraulic fracture which is filled by proppant laden slurry . It is shorter during fracture propagation than the fracture half_length as the propped slurry follows a gel volume w/o proppant , the "clean" fluid
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Propped Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length measured in a radial direction.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Radial Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Radius of an entity with a spherical or cylindrical shape, such as the borehole, an item of drillstring equipment, etc.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Radius

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Horizontal (x-y) distance from origin of position in a receiver line.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Receiver Line Rho

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Horizontal (x-y) distance from origin of true position in a receiver line.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: True Receiver Line Position Rho

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Horizontal (x-y) distance from origin of downhole receiver.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Receiver Orientation Rho

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of semi-major axis of an ellipse; in geodetic work, of a reference ellipsoid.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Semi Major Axis

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of semi-minor axis of an ellipse; in geodetic work, of a reference ellipsoid.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Semi Minor Axis

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Horizontal (x-y) distance from origin of position in a source line.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Source Line Rho

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Horizontal (x-y) distance from origin of true position in a source line.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: True Source Line Position Rho

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Horizontal (x-y) distance from origin of downhole source.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Source Orientation Rho

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Magnitude of uncertainty for a measurement being represented as a position in 2D or 3D coordinate space, such as a geographical position.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Radius of Uncertainty

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Radius of the open borehole. Normally taken as the radius of the drillbit.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Borehole Radius

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Radius of the circle whose arc would have a given curvature.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Radius of Curvature

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Radius of the gooseneck in a Coil Tubing Unit, along which the tubing is bent; used in the fatigue model
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gooseneck Radius

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The difference between the actual radius of an object and its average radius; for boreholes, 1/2 bit size may be used instead of the average radius.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Differential Radius

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The radius of the ellipse of uncertainty cone at the surface location
listOfChildMeasurements.name: EOU Cone Surface Radius

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of the semi-major axis of the reference ellipsoid.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Ellipsoid Semi-major Axis

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of the semi-minor axis of the reference ellipsoid.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Ellipsoid Semi-minor Axis

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The radius of the "invaded zone", the region in which drilling mud filtrate has invaded porous and permeable rock around the borehole.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Invasion Radius

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The radius of a circle (or cylinder) which has the primary influence on a measurement; material or objects outside the Investigation_Radius have little or no effect on the measurement.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Investigation Radius

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Radial distance of the origin of a Local Coordinate System, measured with respect to the origin of the "from" coordinate system. Units, if any, are those of the "from" system.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Origin Rho

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The distance between two features in a reservoir, for use in modeling the reservoir.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Reservoir Distance

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The distance between the well trajectory and the adjacent reservoir boundary distance.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Well-Boundary Distance

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The distance between the sealing fault and the well trajectory.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Well-Fault Distance

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Distance from Borehole to start of fracture element
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Well-Fracture Element Distance

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average distance between two wells, connected or not to regulatory petroleum laws
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Well Spacing

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The characteristic radius of a reservoir used to quantify the behavior of a reservoir. This is the radius that a reservoir would have if circular in shape.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Effective Reservoir Radius

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The characteristic radius to the outer drainage boundary of a field or a reservoir
listOfChildMeasurements.name: External Drainage Radius

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Distance from Horizontal Well to bottom of the Hydraulic Unit
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Horizontal Well Standoff

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Distance from Top of Hydraulic Unit to Top of Flowing Interval
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Distance Hydraulic Unit Top To Flowing Top

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Distance from Top of Hydraulic Unit to Top of Perforation
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Distance Formation Top To Perf Top

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Inter-well distance for a horizontal interference test
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Inter-well Distance

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The length distance between two parallel boundaries in a rectangular reservoir model.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Rectangle Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The width distance between two parallel boundaries in a rectangular reservoir model.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Rectangle Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: K Factor, a function of the geometry of the electrode or sensor array of a resistivity measurement device.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: K Factor

listOfChildMeasurements.description: A measure of surface irregularity, such as of the borehole wall.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Rugosity/Roughness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average amplitude of rugosity, such as the variations in the radius of tubing.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Absolute Roughness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Sum of all the displacements in one direction (generally downhole) made by a downhole equipment. Used as fatigue indicator or charged item in coil tubing operations.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Running Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Distance from the bottom of the Equipment to the Reference Point. The Reference_Point is the origin of the From_Offset distance for an Equipment mounted in From_Mounting_Location=Outside or Inside. The default position for the Reference point is the bottom end of the Equipment. The Reference point is used in drilling to save repositioning all the sensors mounted inside a tool when the end is remachined. There is just one reference point for any equipment mounted on this To_Equipment.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Reference Point Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of one section, such as the nominal length of one section of a streamer.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Section Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The distance between source and receiver or geophone (seismic).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Seismic Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The distance to the seismic source from some other object, such as a wellbore in VSP work.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Source Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In seismic work, the offset at which the reflection time equals the refraction time.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Critical Distance

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Nominal in-line offset between the sources and the first receiver group on each cable (for symmetric configurations)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Nominal Near Trace Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The distance to a seismic receiver from some other object, such as a wellbore in VSP work.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Receiver Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of the equipment shank; for a drill bit, it is the distance from the face of the bit connection to the base of the bit leg (for roller cone bits) or bit crown (for fixed cutter bits).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Shank Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: (Fracturing) Volume of fluid flowing through a given area of porous media which leaks off during the formation of the filter cake. Spurt loss reduces the fluid volume available for fracture extension. Typical Unit: gal/100ft2.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Spurt

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length from the mid-point of the first stabilizer to the bottom connection of the tool
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stab To Bot Conn 1

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length from the mid-point of the second stabilizer to the bottom connection of the tool
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stab To Bot Conn 2

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The amount of elongation observed in an object as a result of its being placed under tension.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stretch

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of stroke (maximum travel), such as for a pump piston or for hydraulic jars).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stroke Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Up stroke distance, as used for drilling jars. Maximum stroke travel in shock/cushion sub
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Up Stroke

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Down stroke distance, as used for drilling jars.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Down Stroke

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length from the mid-point of the third stabilizer to the bottom connection of the tool
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stab To Bot Conn 3

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The amount of physical separation between two objects, usually maintained in order to control their interaction.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Standoff

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Standoff of Perforation Gun
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Perforation Gun Standoff

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The distance from a sensor to the medium being investigated, such as from a logging sonde to the wall of the borehole.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Sensor Standoff

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The distance from the mid-point of the sub tubular equipment to the bottom of the super tubular equipment where the sub tubular equipment is attached.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Tubular String Component Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The smallest of three dimensions {length, width, and thickness}
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Loss of thickness due to any action such as corrosion or erosion
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Wall Thickness Loss

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Depth difference between trough and peak where trough occurs first in increasing depth
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Trough Peak Delta Depth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Depth difference between successive troughs
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Trough Trough Delta Depth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Layer thickness measurement along the borehole, neither corrected for borehole deviation nor for layer dips
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Apparent Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average thickness of a geologic bed.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Average Bed Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Thickness of the cement sheath between casing and borehole wall.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Cement Sheath Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Thickness of hydraulic unit actually contributing to the production.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Completed Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Thickness of the near-wellbore Damaged Zone, the sandface layer around the wellbore where permeability and mobility are impaired, generally by a damaging material (e.g. completion or drilling fluid).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Damaged Zone Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Thickness of the Crushed Zone around perforation
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Crushed Zone Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Filter cake thickness in API test
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Filter Cake Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Thickness of filter cake produced under high temperature, high pressure (HTHP) conditions.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: HTHP Filter Cake Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Thickness of filter cake produced under low temperature, low pressure (LTLP) conditions.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: LTLP Filter Cake Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Total thickness of a zone or a collection of zones, including portions which may not be of interest; may still be subject to discriminator cutoffs specified as "Initial".
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gross Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Total thickness for given lithology in a reservoir summation interval.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Litho Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Maximum thickness, as for a reservoir unit.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Maximum Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Total Net Pay hydrocarbon porosity-thickness for all zones; that portion of Net_Pay_Porosity_Thickness which is hydrocarbon-filled.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Net Pay HC Porosity Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The net pay moved hydrocarbon volume multiplied by the net pay thickness; the portion of Net Pay Porosity Thickness filled with moved hydrocarbons.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Net Pay Moved Hydrocarbon Porosity Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Total net pay porosity-thickness of the zone interval: the product of Net Pay Thickness and Net Pay Average Porosity
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Net Pay Porosity Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The cumulative thickness of hydrocarbon bearing rocks which satisfy local criteria for a "pay zone"; the footage which satisfies the Net Reservoir conditions and where the water saturation cutoff, permeability cutoff and any discriminator cutoffs specified as "Net Pay" are satisfied; abbreviated "H" for a Hydraulic Unit.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Net Pay Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Total Net Reservoir hydrocarbon porosity-thickness for all zones; that portion of Net_Reservoir_Porosity_Thickness which is hydrocarbon-filled.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Net Reservoir HC Porosity Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: It is common in an interbedded reservoir for sands thinner than a certain cutoff thickness (Min_Net_Thickness) to be discarded as non net or non pay in a ResSum type analysis. However, a thick sand may have two closely spaced shale stringers, such that they create the effect of a thin sand separated from thick sands above and below by thin shale beds. In this case, if the shale beds are thinner than a second thickness threshold (Min_Non_Net_Thickness), the thin sand would be counted as net or pay.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Minimum Net Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: It is common in an interbedded reservoir for sands thinner than a certain cutoff thickness (Min_Net_Thickness) to be discarded as non net or non pay in a ResSum type analysis. However, a thick sand may have two closely spaced shale stringers, such that they create the effect of a thin sand separated from thick sands above and below by thin shale beds. In this case, if the shale beds are thinner than a second thickness threshold (Min_Non_Net_Thickness), the thin sand would be counted as net or pay.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Minimum Non-net Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Minimum thickness, as for a reservoir unit. Also used for stress calculation with coiled tubing, with data supplied by the manufacturer
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Minimum Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Total pore thickness of the zone; i.e. the product of Porosity and Net_Reservoir_Thickness.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Net Reservoir Porosity Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Total thickness of the portion of the zone which has porosity suitable to be a potential reservoir; i.e. the footage which satisfies the Net Thickness conditions and where the porosity cutoff and any discriminator cutoffs specified as "Net Reservoir" are satisfied.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Net Reservoir Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Difference between Gross_Thickness and Net_Thickness; i.e. the thickness of the formations excluded from "Net" due to cutoff for maximum clay content.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Net Shale Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Total thickness of the non-shales in the interval; i.e. total footage where the clay volume cutoff and any discriminator cutoffs specified as Net are satisfied.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Net Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Nominal thickness
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Nominal thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Depth difference between successive peaks
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Peak Peak Delta Depth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Depth difference between peak and trough where peak occurs first in increasing depth
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Peak Trough Delta Depth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Total flowing thickness along the Borehole ("Hp")
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Producing Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Cumulative thickness of an earth layer, measured perpendicular to the bedding plane, thus eliminating any offset effect due to borehole deviation or structural dip. Also called True Bed Thickness.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: True Stratigraphic Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Isochores obtained by correcting for structural dip in order to account for the lateral offset of the intersections of the well bore with the top and bottom of a layer.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: True Vertical Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Wall thickness of tube or body of equipment item.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Tube Wall Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Distance from the bottom (make-up plane) of the gun or the assembly of guns to the upper perforating charge
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Top Charge Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of a trace or mark which is visible on some surface, such as that of a road on a map, or of a fracture on a borehole wall.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Trace Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of material which has been cut away either to prevent fatigue rupture on a cable or a coiled tubing or to connect an equipment
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Trimmed Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Shot position relative to the CDP Line
listOfChildMeasurements.name: True Common Depthpoint Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Vertical Section, historical name given to the horizontal distance from the surface location to the downhole point (horizontal counterpart to True Vertical Depth).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Vertical Section

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Bottom "depth" of an interval along a Vertical Section (VSCT) index.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Vertical Section

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Top "depth" of an interval along a Vertical Section (VSCT) index.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Vertical Section

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The wave length of the sinusoidal function fitting the deviation survey station points and simulating a real well path
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Wellbore Tortuosity Wave Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Wheel Circumference
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Wheel Circumference

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The measurement taken at right angles to the length.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The size of any opening in an otherwise solid wall or surface. The size of a window that limits the information affecting a measuring device. Also used in processing (e.g., seismic migration or deconvolution.)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Aperture Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Width of the blade at gauge, as used for drill stabilizer blades.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Blade Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The perpendicular distance between two parallel boundaries.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Channel Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Width of formation etched (dissolved) by reaction with acid on the fracture face (Acid fracturing)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Etched Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Width of fracture element
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Fracture Element Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The distance between adjacent fractures.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Facture Spacing

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Width of a fracture.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Facture Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: For core images, the width of the core which is hidden on the left side of the image (by core box, for example).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Left Hidden Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Width of the proppant laden volume within an hydraulic fracture (hydraulic fracturing). Smaller during fracture propagation than the fracture width.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Propped Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Width between flanges of the drum core, such as for a coiled tubing reel
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Core Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: For core images, the width of the core which is hidden on the right side of the image (by core box, for example).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Right Hidden Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Width of a slot, such as in a slotted liner.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Slot Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The size of the aperture of the trace on the borehole surface
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Trace Aperture

listOfChildMeasurements.description: For core images, the width of the core which is visible in the image.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Visible Width

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of frequency filter
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Frequency Filter Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length of Optical Wave
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Optical Wave Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length applied in seismic migration
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Migration_Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Describes the volume per area. E.g. the quantity of hydrocarbons generated in an area
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Volume Per Area

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The product of the Storativity of a layer and its thickness [phi*Ct*h].
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Storativity-Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Sum of the Storativity_Thickness values of all layers in the model.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Total Storativity-Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Inter-well Storativity-Thickness [phi*Ct*h] for a horizontal interference test.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Inter-well Storativity-Thickness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: A measure of the effect of the medium on the magnetic field, B, when subject to a magnetizing force, H; B = Mu0 * (H + M), where Mu0 is the permeability of free space.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Magnetization

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Magnetic Field Strength along the X-axis.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: X Magnetometer

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Magnetic Field Strength along the Y-axis.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Y Magnetometer

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Magnetic Field Strength along the Z-axis.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Z Magnetometer

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Magnetic Pole Strength
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Magnetic_Pole_Strength

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Magnetic Pole Strength
listOfChildMeasurements.name: MagneticPoleStrength

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Use for espressing the strength of the earth's magnetic field
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Nano_Tesla

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Use for espressing the strength of the earth's magnetic field
listOfChildMeasurements.name: NanoTesla

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Use for product of pipe linear mass by length
listOfChildMeasurements.name: High_Mass

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Use for product of pipe linear mass by length
listOfChildMeasurements.name: HighMass

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Weight of material unavailable for use remaining in a container
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Dead Weight

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Weight of Material
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Material Weight

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Sack "weight" (mass) to which unit by sack refers e.g. lbs/sack
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Reference Sack Weight

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Mass of proppant per fracture area (hydraulic fracturing)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Proppant Areal Distribution

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Specific acoustic impedance is a ratio of acoustic pressure to specific flow, or flow per unit area, or flow velocity.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: SpecificAcousticImpedance

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Property which controls the propagation of an ultrasonic wave in a medium. It is the product of the material density and the acoustic wave velocity within the material.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Acoustic Impedance

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The specific acoustic impedance is a ratio of acoustic pressure to specific flow, or flow per unit area, or flow velocity.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Specific Acoustic Impedance

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Interface property which is the difference between the Acoustic Impedance values of two adjacent beds.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Acoustic Contrast

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Property which controls the propagation of a seismic wave at a particular (non-zero) angle of incidence. It is a function of the material density, the compressional wave velocity within the material, the ratio between the shear and the compressional wave velocities, and the angle of incidence. This property, analogous to Acoustic_Impedance but for non-zero incidence angles, is described in 1998 SEG Paper "Calibration and Inversion of Non-Zero Offset Seismic Data", by Patrick Connolly (BP).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Elastic Impedance

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The mass per area versus geologic time. E.g. generated mass of hydrocarbons per area of a source rock per million years
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mass Per Area Per Geologic Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Weight of an object or material per unit length; commonly used for tubular goods like casing, tubing, drill pipe, etc.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Linear Weight

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The weight of a tubular such as casing or drillpipe that has been calculated based on a formula involving diameter and wall thickness of the tubular.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Nominal Weight

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Scale deposit per length
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Scale Deposit per Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The property of a substance offering internal resistance to flow; a measure of the degree of fluidity.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The viscosity of water at specific temperature and pressure conditions.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Water Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Ratio Shear Stress/Shear Rate. Equal to Newtonian Viscosity for Newtonian fluid.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Apparent Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The viscosity of the fluid filtrate i.e the viscosity of the fluid which crossed the filtering media.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Filtrate Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The viscosity of a fluid (sample) at specific temperature and pressure conditions.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Fluid Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The viscosity of a gas at specific temperature and pressure conditions.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gas Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The viscosity of a liquid at specific temperature and pressure conditions.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Liquid Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Slope of Shear Stress/Shear Rate curve for the Newtonian rheology model (Shear Stress proportional to Shear Rate)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Newtonian Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The viscosity of oil at specific temperature and pressure conditions.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Oil Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Apparent viscosity of the Bingham Plastic model : Slope of the curve shear stress vs. shear rate (rheogram). Model equation is Shear_Stress = Yield_Stress + Plastic_Viscosity times Shear_Rate.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Plastic Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Measure of the internal resistance to fluid flow attributable to the amount, type, and size of solids present in a given fluid. When using the direct-indicating viscometer, it is found by subtracting the 300-rpm reading from the 600-rpm reading of a Fann35 rheometer.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: API Plastic Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Measure of the internal resistance to fluid flow attributable to the amount, type, and size of solids present in a given fluid. The Casson model equation is: SQRT(Shear_Stress) = SQRT(Yield_Stress) + SQRT(Plastic_Viscosity X Shear_Rate)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Casson Plastic Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The viscosity of reservoir fluid at specific temperature and pressure conditions.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Reservoir Fluid Viscosity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: A measure of flow rate expressed as mass of material per unit time.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mass Flowrate

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Mass flowrate of oil.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Oil Mass Flowrate

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Mass flowrate of water.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Water Mass Flowrate

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Mass per time for large quantities
listOfChildMeasurements.name: High Mass Per Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Mass flowrate of gas.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gas Mass Flowrate

listOfChildMeasurements.description: A measure of the mass produced, say from some facility, per unit time.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Throughput

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Mass per geologic time. E.g. the generated mass of hydrocarbons per geologic time
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mass Per Geologic Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The density (mass per unit volume) of a material. Usually at Standard conditions (STP). Also used to indicate the frequency of occurrence.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The density of mud, or drilling fluid, used during drilling operations.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mud Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The mud density that initiates formation shear or tensile failure.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Critical Mud Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Drilling fluid density that would be required to produce the same effective borehole pressure as the combination of fluid density, circulating pressure and cuttings loading of the drilling fluid in the wellbore.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Equivalent Circulating Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Equivalent mud weight determined by the formation integrity test (FIT) for a new formation below last casing shoe via increasing the pressure until a pre-determined value.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: FIT EMW

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Equivalent mud weight determined by the leak off test (LOT) for a new formation below last casing shoe via increasing the pressure until the formation starts taking fluid.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: LOT EMW

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Maximum allowable mud density
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Max Mud Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average value of the material density.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Average Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Density of bulk material, including any void space or other materials contained in the subject volume. In well logging, it is the density of the rock, including fluid-filled pore space, as measured with a "Gamma-Gamma" type logging device.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Bulk Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Correction to the Bulk Density log, as measured with a Gamma-gamma type logging device; used as an indication of hole condition to validate the Bulk_Density measurement; conventionally abbreviated DRHO.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Delta-Rho

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Electron density. Gamma-gamma logging techniques respond to electron density, which is near bulk density for most formation types.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Electron Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Formation density as measured with a Litho-Density or Gamma-Gamma type logging tool; conventionally abbreviated RHOB.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Litho Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The density or weight per unit volume of cement (or cement slurry).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Cement Density/Weight

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Density of the input material, such as the drilling fluid in the mixing tank.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Density In

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Density of the output fluid, such as the drilling fluid returning from the well annulus.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Density Out

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Density of the filter cake (mudcake).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Filter Cake Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Density of a fluid sample; e.g., from Borehole, Formations, Cores, etc. Also density of cement.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Fluid Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Bulk density of the solid frame of the rock. The solid frame of the rock includes the porosity but not the content of the pore spaces. Frame_Density = (1 - Porosity) * Grain_Density.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Frame Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Density of gas (air, hydrocarbon, etc.) at a particular temperature and/or pressure; e.g., gas density at well bottomhole conditions or at well surface conditions.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gas Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The density of a unit volume of a mineral or other rock material at zero porosity. Sometimes called Matrix Density.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Grain Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average grain density in the Net Reservoir portion of the summation interval, computed from core data by point-match method.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Net Reservoir Core Grain Density (PM)

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average grain density in the Net Reservoir portion of the summation interval, computed from log data by point-match method.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Net Reservoir Log Grain Density (PM)

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Density of hydrocarbons.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Hydrocarbon Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Interval value of the material density (density for a layer).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Interval Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Synonym of Grain_Density. The density of the material in a porous system that is not within the pores.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Matrix Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Maximum density
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Maximum Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Minimum density
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Minimum Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The density of a mineral.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mineral Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Apparent density of a component (fluid, gas, etc.) in the presence of other components. The sum of the partial densities equals total density.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Partial Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The density of oil.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Oil Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The density of the proppant material
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Proppant Density/Weight

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The density of the reservoir fluid i.e. the mixture oil, gas and water.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Reservoir

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The density of water.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Water Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Liquid density
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Liquid Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Reservoir mass density
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Reservoir Mass Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Slurry density
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Slurry Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: CaCl2 concentration.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: CaCl2 Concentration

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Calcium concentration (Water Based Mud and water phase for Oil Based Mud)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Calcium Concentration

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Filtrate CaCl2 concentration in the water phase of Oil Based Mud
listOfChildMeasurements.name: CaCl2 Aqueous

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Magnesium concentration in a material.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Magnesium Concentration

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Proppant concentration expressed as mass of proppant added per gallon of gel, legacy (LIS) unit "PPA"
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Proppant Concentration

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Sum of Ca and Mg concentration in water, API RP13B, Section 8, Water Based Mud, expressed as being entirely composed of calcium
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Total Hardness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Concentration of material in a sample expressed as mass of the material per unit volume of sample.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mass Concentration

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Ratio between solid additive mass and fluid volume
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gel Mass Concentration

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Concentration of material in a sample expressed as mass of the material per unit volume of gas sample.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gas Mass Concentration

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Rate of fluid produced per unit change in limiting pressure per unit of reservoir thickness. For oil wells, PIs is normally expressed in barrels per day per psi per foot of net reservoir thickness.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Specific Productivity Index

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Mobility of the near-wellbore Damaged Zone, the sandface layer around the wellbore where permeability and mobility are impaired, generally by a damaging material (e.g. completion or drill mud).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Damaged Zone Mobility

listOfChildMeasurements.description: A measure of the ease with which a fluid can be moved horizontally in a specific medium (i.e. rock). The ratio of the effective horizontal permeability and the viscosity of the fluid.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Horizontal Mobility

listOfChildMeasurements.description: A measure of the ease with which a fluid can be moved in a specific medium (i.e. rock); computed as the cube root of (Vertical_Mobility X Horizontal_Mobility**2)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Spherical Mobility

listOfChildMeasurements.description: A measure of the ease with which a fluid can be moved vertically in a specific medium (i.e. rock). The ratio of the effective vertical permeability and the viscosity of the fluid.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Vertical Mobility

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The ratio of the number of moles of a material in a sample to the volume of the sample.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Molar Concentration

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Number of moles of a material per unit volume.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Molar Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Number of moles of a liquid material per unit volume.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Liquid Molar Density

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The rate at which optical enery is emitted or transferred.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Optical Power

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The maximum reading (deflection) taken from a direct-reading viscometer after the fluid has been quiescent for 10 minutes.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gel Test Deflection - 10min

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The maximum reading (deflection) taken from a direct-reading viscometer after the fluid has been quiescent for 10 seconds.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gel Test Deflection - 10s

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The maximum reading (deflection) taken from a direct-reading viscometer after the fluid has been quiescent for 1 minutes.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gel Test Deflection - 1min

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The maximum reading (deflection) taken from a direct-reading viscometer after the fluid has been quiescent for 30 minutes.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gel Test Deflection - 30min

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Horizontal angle measured clockwise from true North. (Also referred to as True Bearing.) Occasionally azimuth will be specified relative to some other reference.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The azimuth of the point at which borehole failure starts.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Borehole Failure Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of central line of projection.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Central Line Bearing

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The azimuth of an object with respect to magnetic north.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Compass Bearing

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of the direction of maximum dip of a surface; dip may be computed in several ways, including from logs, from well-to-well correlation, from gradients on interpreted time or depth surfaces, etc.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Dip Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of formation dip relative to structural dip; computed by subtracting structural dip from true dip (dip removal).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Relative Dip Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In the plane perpendicular to the borehole, viewed from above the tool, angle measured clockwise from the projection of the north direction to the projection of the true dip azimuth.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Apparent Dip Azimuth wrt North

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In the plane perpendicular to the borehole, viewed from above the tool, angle measured clockwise from logging tool reference direction to the projection of the true dip azimuth.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Apparent Dip Azimuth wrt Tool Reference

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In the plane perpendicular to the borehole, viewed from above the tool, angle measured clockwise from the top of hole direction to the projection of the true dip azimuth.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Apparent Dip Azimuth wrt Top Of Hole

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of the direction to an axis, usually pertaining to a sedimentary channel.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Direction of Channel To Axis

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of the direction to flow, usually pertaining to a sedimentary channel.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Direction of Channel To Flow

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of the direction to land, usually pertaining to a sedimentary channel.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Direction of Channel To Land

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The azimuth of the flow direction that insured transportation an deposition of the sediments.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Direction of Current

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of the direction to the downthrown block in case of faulting in the Earth subsurface.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Direction To Downthrown Block

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of the direction of overthrust in case of faulting in the Earth subsurface.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Direction Of Overthrust

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The direction from which sediments are brought
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Direction to Source

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of the line from the center of an area to an eccentered object.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Eccentering Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The azimuth of a fracture usually in an interval of the borehole.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Facture Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The azimuth of the strike of a fault.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Fault Strike

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The azimuth of a point on an object corresponding to the origin of an image of the object (left side of core image)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Origin Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The orientation of a fracture relative to north.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Fracture Orientation

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The azimuth of a plane represented by a great circle.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Great Circle Dip Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The angle between a vertical plane tangent to the borehole and north.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Wellbore Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The horizontal angle measured from a meridian to the direction of magnetic north as determined by a freely suspended magnet. Positive if magnetic North is east of True North.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Magnetic Declination

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Major axis Azimuth of the ellipse of uncertainty (related parameter: EOU_MAJOR_AXIS_AZIM)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Major Axis Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The minimum horizontal stress azimuth with respect to true north.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Minimum Horizontal Stress Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Shear energy polarization azimuth angle measured clockwise from grid north.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Polarization Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Estimation of the polarization azimuth angle for all layers to the current dept.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stack Polarization Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Estimation of the polarization azimuth angle for a layer.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Interval Polarization Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of positive y-axis of projection.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Projection Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Projection relative bearing
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Projection Relative Bearing

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Raw relative bearing
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Raw Relative Bearing

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of the direction to which the rig is facing.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Rig Heading

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The azimuth of a sensor on a logging device, used to determine the orientation of the device.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Sensor Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The azimuth of the pole associated with a small circle.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Small Circle Dip Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of the thin out of a barrier type depositional environment.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Thin-out Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle measured clockwise from North to the horizontal projection of the radius passing through the tool angle reference point. One of Tool_Azimuth or Relative_Bearing must be present
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Tool Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The Azimuth coordinate of a trace
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Trace Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Fastest direction of elliptic anisotropic velocity (i.e. ellipse major axis) measured clockwise from grid north in degrees.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Velocity Ellipticity Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Estimation of the velocity ellipticity azimuth angle for a layer
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Interval Velocity Ellipticity Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Estimation of the velocity ellipticity azimuth for all layers to the current depth.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stack Velocity Ellipticity Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle between the true north and the vertical section plane.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Vertical Section Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of the direction from which the waves are coming.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Wave Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of the direction from which the wind is blowing.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Wind Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Azimuth of the axis, usually pertaining to a depositional environment such as a tidal-flat.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Axis Azimuth

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The horizontal angle between the direction to a point and the direction of some reference line, normally measured as a clockwise angle from the reference line.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Bearing

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle of first bend in equipment item.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Bend 1 Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Maximum first bent angle
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Max Bend 1 Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle between the planes defined by the first and second bends in the equipment string.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Bend 1-2 Offset Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle of second bend in equipment item.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Bend 2 Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Maximum second bent angle
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Max Bend 2 Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle between the planes defined by the second and third bends in the equipment string.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Bend 2-3 Offset Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle between Binset axes measured counterclockwise from positive X axis to positive Y axis
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Binset Skew

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Degree of spiral blade coverage 0, 270, 450, -270. (0-straight blade; Negative-left spiral; Positive-right spiral)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Blade Spiral

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In directional drilling, the angle between a (sensor-bearing) stabilizer blade and a fixed reference, measured in a plane normal to the drillstring. In near-vertical applications, North is the fixed reference (Magnetic_Bladeface); for higher deviation applications, Top of Hole is the reference (Gravity_Bladeface).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Bladeface

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In directional drilling, the angle between Top of Hole and a sensor contained in a stabilizer blade; used in hole sections of high deviation. Measurement is from -180 to +180 degrees.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gravity Bladeface

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In directional drilling, the angle between Magnetic North and a sensor contained in a stabilizer blade; Measurement represents an Azimuth, with values from 0 to 360 degrees.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Magnetic Bladeface

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The angle between the celestial equator and a celestial body, measured along a great circle passing through the celestial poles.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Declination

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle of incidence for which a refracted ray follows the surface of contact between two media of different velocities.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Critical Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angular departure from some reference direction. When used with wells, it is the angle between the borehole axis and the vertical (also known as the Drift Angle).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Deviation

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle between the borehole axis and the vertical (also known as the Drift Angle and, in the drilling industry, Inclination).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Deviation

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Maximum deviation value of the wellbore from the vertical
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Maximum Wellbore Deviation

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Inclination of the drillstring as measured as the bit
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Bit Inclination

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Inclination of the drillstring as measured downhole
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Downhole Inclination

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle between the tool axis and the vertical.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Tool Deviation

listOfChildMeasurements.description: X-axis component of the angle between the tool axis and the vertical.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Deviation X

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Y-axis component of the angle between the tool axis and the vertical.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Deviation Y

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle relating the increase in volumetric strain with stress.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Dilation Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The maximum vertical angle that a surface; e.g. a bedding or fault surface, makes with the horizontal, measured perpendicular to the strike direction of the structure. Dip may be computed in several ways, including from logs, from well-to-well correlation, from gradients on interpreted time or depth surfaces (See Time_Dip and Depth_Dip), etc.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Dip Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The dip of the plane represented by a great circle.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Great Circle Dip Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle that a surface, e.g. a bedding or fault surface, makes with the horizontal, measured in the in-line direction.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Inline Dip

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Estimation of the inline dip for all layers to the current depth.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stack Inline Dip

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Estimation of the inline dip for a layer.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Interval Inline Dip

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Magnitude of formation dip relative to structural dip; computed by subtracting structural dip from true dip (dip removal).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Relative Dip Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The angle of the pole associated with a small circle.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Small Circle Dip Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle between the dip plane and the plane perpendicular to the borehole
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Apparent Dip Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle that a surface, e.g. a bedding or fault surface, makes with the horizontal, measured in the cross-line direction.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Crossline Dip

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Estimation of the crossline dip for a layer.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Interval Crossline Dip

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Estimation of the crossline dip for all layers to the current depth.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stack Crossline Dip

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Offset in azimuth due to eccentering; used to convert azimuth values with respect to an eccentered position into azimuth values relative to center.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Eccentering Azimuth Offset

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The portion of the borehole circumference that has failed, expressed as the angle subtended by the arc length of the failure.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Failure Arc

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The angle that a fault plane makes with the vertical.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Fault Hade

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle between riser and blowout preventer at the flex joint.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Flex Joint Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The angle which the raypath of an incident ray makes with the perpendicular to the interface. In an isotropic medium, it is the same as the angle that a wavefront makes with the interface.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Incident Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle relating the increase in shear strength with compressive strength.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Friction Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The pole to a plane represented by a great circle.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Great Circle Dip Axis

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle to be used in converting azimuths between true north and grid north or the Y axis of the cartographic projection. [Geoshare convention: True Azimuth = Grid Azimuth + Grid_Convergence_Angle]
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Grid Convergence Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Phase component of an analytical seismic trace when decomposed into amplitude and phase components (Hilbert transform technique)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Instantaneous Phase

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Instantaneous phase at maximum of reflection strength. Similar to Response_Phase, but with maximum within a user-defined interval.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Phase at Envelope Maximum

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Instantaneous phase at local maximum of reflection intensity
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Response Phase

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The smallest angle between two intersecting sealing faults in a wedge well test model.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Interfault Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The vertical angle between a line and the horizontal; has historically been used in the drilling industry to mean the angle between the borehole path and vertical (the term Hole_Deviation is preferred for this concept).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Inclination

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The vertical angle measured between the horizontal plane and the direction of magnetic north as determined by a freely suspended magnet. Sometimes known as magnetic dip. Positive values if the direction to magnetic north is below the horizon.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Magnetic Inclination

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Maximum inclination of sensor
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Maximum Inclination

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Vertical angle of downhole receiver, measured from the x-y plane.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Receiver Orientation Phi

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Vertical angle of downhole source, measured from the x-y plane.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Inclination

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Angle of the screen, with respect to horizontal
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Screen Angle

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Vertical inclination of the ellipses of uncertainties relative to the wellbore at the associated survey point.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Vertical Rotation

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The angle between the axis of the Earth and a tangent to the ellipsoid which approximates the shape of the Earth.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Latitude

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Latitude of Northing reference point.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Northing Latitude

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The latitude of the point of origin of an orthogonal grid constructed on a map projection. Frequently this is a projection standard parallel, but can be any defined latitude.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Origin Latitude

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Latitude at which scale factor is exact.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Scale Factor Latitude

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Latitude of parallel along which scale is true.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Standard Parallel

listOfChildMeasurements.description: First line of latitude along which scale is true, for map projections using two standard parallels; this parallel is NEAREST to the EQUATOR.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Standard Parallel 1

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Second line of latitude along which scale is true, for map projections using two standard parallels; this parallel is NEAREST to the POLE.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Standard Parallel 2

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Latitude at which scale is true, as with a standard parallel.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Latitude True Scale Latitude

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Latitude value used as the basis or starting point, such as in a multiple regression computation.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Base Latitude

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Latitude of first point on central line of projection.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Latitude of Central Line Point 1

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Latitude of second point on central line of projection.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Latitude of Central Line Point 2

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stack Anisotropic Axis 1 Inline Direction

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Anisotropic Axis 2 Inline Direction

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Estimation of the anisotropic axis 2 inline direction for a layer.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Interval Anisotropic Axis 2 Inline Direction

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Estimation of the anisotropic axis 2 inline direction for all layers to the current depth.

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Embedment Strength

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The maximum tensile stress a material can tolerate without splitting
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Tensile Strength

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gas Differential Pressure

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Maximum Differential Pressure
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Max Differential Pressure

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Elastic Modulus

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Bulk Modulus: k

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Frame Bulk Modulus

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Downstream Coil Working Pressure

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Maximum allowable pressure for the equipment

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Maximum water pressure

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Hydraulic pressure exerted on a formation during a fracturing job (fracture pressure) minus Closure Pressure.

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Mud pump maximum discharge pressure
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mud Pump Maximum Discharge Pressure

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The difference between input and output pressure, usually due to friction.

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The nominal pressure loss in a piece of equipment, such as a Drill_Motor or an MWD_Tool.

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Deep Laterolog Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Resistivity measurement which has been compensated for the dielectric constant of the formation..
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Dielectric Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Propagation Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Phase Shift Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Formation resistivity as measured by the attenuation of a high frequency (hundreds of KHz to several MHz) electromagnetic wave; these measurements are typically deeper than measurements based on phase shift, but their vertical resolution is less sharp and they often cannot be used reliably in high-resistivity formations.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Attenuation Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Resistivity of the formation flushed zone (that portion of the formation in which the movable fluids are considered to have been completely replaced by mud filtrate during drilling).

listOfChildMeasurements.description: True Formation Resistivity
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Formation Resistivity (Rt)

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Formation resistivity measured parallel to layering. (for "Transverse-Isotropic (TI)" rock"
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Horizontal Resistivity (Rh)

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Formation resistivity measured perpendicular to layering. (for "Transverse-Isotropic (TI)" rock
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Vertical Resistivity (Rv)

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Resistivity of Mud Filter Cake
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mud Filter Cake Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Medium Induction Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Micro Cylindrically Focused Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Micro Resistivity measurement using an "inverse" lateral electrode arrangement; traditionally combined with Micro Normal Resistivity in a Microlog survey for identifying permeable beds.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Micro Inverse Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Resistivity measurement using a "lateral" electrode arrangement with a very shallow investigation radius (1-2 inches into the formation).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Micro Lateral Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: A measurement of the resistivity of the formation, by a laterolog (or guard log) resistivity device, within the first few inches of the borehole wall.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Micro Laterolog Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Micro Resistivity measurement using a "normal" electrode arrangement; traditionally combined with Micro Inverse Resistivity in a Microlog survey for identifying permeable beds.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Micro Normal Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Mineral Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The resistivity which represents a measurement made approximately one to two feet into the formation; generally considered to measure the formation where it contains fluids which are comprised primarily of mud filtrate.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Shallow Resistivity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The resistivity, measured by an induction log, which represents a measurement made approximately one to two feet into the formation; generally considered to measure the formation where it contains fluids which are comprised primarily of mud filtrate.

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Time needed for a given quantity of fluid (generally a quart of mud) to flow into a specified size funnel (3/16 inch id tube of a 12 inch long funnel). Used for drilling fluids.

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Residual static information (time) for each station

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The time for the neutron population to fall to 1/e (37%) of its original value. Commonly called Tau, it is inversely related to Neutron_Capture_Cross_Section

listOfChildMeasurements.description: A time value which is intended to indicate the duration of a process or event.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Time Interval

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Listening time until first detection

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Time zone correction (defined to fractions of an hour) to be added to vehicle system time to correct to standard time. (GMT, UTC,...)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Time System Offset Wrt Standard Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Length (time or depth interval) of the crosscorrelation window to use while tracking
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Tracking Operator Length

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Acquisition system transit time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Acoustic transit time (normally a two-way time) from seismic reference datum to the well marker, as picked from a seismic section.

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The elapsed time required for an acoustic wave to travel from one point to another.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Acoustic Travel Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Total acoustic travel time over a wellbore interval as computed by integrating acoustic slowness from a sonic log (Compressional_Slowness) over the interval.

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The time required for an acoustic wave to travel from its source to a reflector and return to a receiver.

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Generic interpretation on seismic traveltime sections

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Aperture Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Computed equivalent operating time based on the time spent at a given temperature and the maximum working temperature. If all the time is spent at maximum working temperature, then the equivalent time is equal to the operating time.

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Cumulative Equivalent Operating Time, called Cumulative Time Usage or CTU.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Cumulative Equivalent Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The time difference by which one event lags another. In refraction seismic work, the additional time required to traverse a raypath over the time which would be required to traverse the horizontal component at the highest velocity encountered on the raypath.

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Maximum Delay Time
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Max Delay Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Minimum Delay Time
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Min Delay Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Time After Bit

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and the point at which the toolface measurement is taken reaching a given point in the wellbore.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Toolface Time After Bit

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a density sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Density Time After Bit

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a gamma ray sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gamma Ray Time After Bit

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a neutron sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Neutron Time After Bit

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a resistivity sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Resistivity Time After Bit

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In MWD/LWD logging, the time delay between the drill bit and a sonic sensor reaching a given point in the wellbore.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Sonic Time After Bit

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Time during which equipment is not operational condition or is otherwise unavailable.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Downtime

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Closure Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Seismic line dependent adjustment to achieve a continuous, line independent reference surface
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Intermediate Time Level

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The time difference between two reflection events. It may vary due to velocity changes in different media, or changes in thickness of strata, or changes following erosion or structural deformation.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Interval Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Maximum time at extreme conditions
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Maximum Extreme Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Scan Time corresponding to the fastest scanning rate supported by the Equipment
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Min Scan Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Equivalent time correction corresponding to the phase corrections. Assumes a specified dominant frequency.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mis-tie Phase Time Equivalent

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Constant time correction to apply to a seismic line to compensate for time differences.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mis-tie Static Correction Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Time correction applicable to each trace on a seismic line.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mis-tie Variable Correction Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The additional time required for energy to travel from a source to a flat reflecting bed and back to a geophone at some distance from the source point compared to the time to return to a geophone at the source point.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Normal Moveout

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Period of time which is spent operating, either for a single operation or for a series of operations. Complement of Idle_Time.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Operating Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Elapsed time during which pumping has taken place.

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Time it takes to pump fluid into the fracture

listOfChildMeasurements.name: Period

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In nuclear magnetic resonance measurements, the time constant related to the rate at which nuclei realign to the static magnetic field after disturbance by a radio frequency pulse.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Relaxation Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Transverse, or spin-spin, relaxation time constant for transverse magnetization decay rate of nuclei; normally abbreviated by symbol T2.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Relaxation Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Longitudinal, or spin-lattice, relaxation time constant for alignment rate of nuclei to static magnetic field; normally abbreviated by symbol T1.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Relaxation Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Time of first measurement for each station since the Origin_Time stored in Seis_Survey_Area
