listOfChildMeasurements.name: Recorder Delay Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Difference between observed refraction traveltime and the traveltime which would have been observed if only one head-wave velocity had been involved.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Reduced Traveltime

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Duration of data sampling or recording.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Sampling Period

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Time interval between the recording of two sequential data samples.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Sampling Period

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Duration (length) in time of the sliding window used for processing.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Sliding Window Duration

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Interval below the picked Z to search for the Tracking Event and Snap_Type when snapping
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Snap Window Bottom

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Interval above the picked Z to search for the Tracking Event and Snap_Type when snapping
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Snap Window Top

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Time elapsed since production conditions were stable
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Elapsed Time at Stable Conditions

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Total amount of mis-tie correction to apply. Evaluated at line ties.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Total Mis-tie Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Time increment between samples indexed by time.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Time Increment

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Uncertainty of a time measurement.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Time Uncertainty

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Exponential decay time constant, also known as mean lifetime, tau and inverse of decay constant (lambda)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Time Constant

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Simulation time
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Simulation Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Inverse of drilling penetration rate.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Inverse Penetration Rate

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Use for Inverse ROP measurements
listOfChildMeasurements.name: InversePenetrationRate

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The transit time interval per unit length of an acoustic wave; inverse of wave velocity. Applies to all types of Delta-T: Compressional, Shear and Stoneley.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Acoustic Slowness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The time it takes for a compressional wave to traverse a fixed distance; reciprocal of Compressional_Velocity.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Compressional Slowness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Acoustic slowness of a fluid; the slowness of the compressional wave.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Fluid Delta-T

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Acoustic compressional slowness (Delta-T) of the drilling fluid.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mud Delta-T

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Acoustic slowness of a compressional wave in a given material or matrix.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Matrix Delta-T

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The acoustic slowness of a Rayleigh wave (type of seismic wave propagated along the free surface of a semi-infinite medium).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Rayleigh Delta-T

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Acoustic slowness of a shear wave (Vs); reciprocal of Shear_Velocity; a shear wave is a type of seismic wave in which the particle motion is perpendicular to the direction of propagation; also called S-wave or secondary wave.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Shear Delta-T

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Acoustic slowness of a shear wave in a given material or matrix.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Matrix Shear Delta-T

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The acoustic slowness of a Stoneley wave; a Stoneley wave is a type of seismic wave which is propagated along an interface, such as a tube wave in a borehole.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stoneley Delta-T

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Acoustic slowness for small quantities
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Low Acoustic Slowness

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Time per unit length required for an electromagnetic wave to propagate over some interval in some medium like air, water, drilling fluid, etc..
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Electromagnetic Propagation Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The time it takes for an electromagnetic wave to traverse a fixed distance of a given material or matrix. In this case the material or matrix is a specific, zero porosity rock, e.g. sandstone, limestone or dolomite.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Matrix Electromagnetic Propagation Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The travel time of a wave over a unit distance, hence the reciprocal of wave velocity.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Interval Transit Time

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Dip computed on a time surface by measuring the difference in seismic times between two points compared to the horizontal distance between the points.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Time Dip

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Dip of seismic data, similar to Time_Dip but gradient derived from the seismic data in time)
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Correlation Time Dip

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The rate at which a drill bit penetrates a particular lithostratigraphic layer; measured in units of time per mass.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Litho Penetration Rate

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Gas D factor
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gas D Factor

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Use for wind and current speeds
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Weather_Speed

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Use for wind and current speeds
listOfChildMeasurements.name: WeatherSpeed

listOfChildMeasurements.description: NMR surface relaxivity
listOfChildMeasurements.name: NMR_Surface_Relaxivity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The velocity of an acoustic wave; the rate at which the wave travels from one point to another. Used generally for all elastic and seismic waves.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Acoustic Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Variation of acoustic velocity with frequency. Dispersion may be normal (velocity decreases with frequency) or inverse (velocity increases with frequency).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Acoustic Dispersion

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Variation of acoustic velocity with direction, distorting the shape of a wavetrain.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Angular Dispersion

listOfChildMeasurements.description: In seismics, the phase velocity which a wavefront appears to have along a line of geophones. Otherwise, the inverse of the slope of a refraction time-distance curve.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Apparent Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average velocity of an acoustic wave: the distance between two points divided by the travel time of the compressional wave between those points.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Average Acoustic Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Special usage of Avg_Acoustic_Velocity which deals specifically with the velocity between a reference datum near the surface and some subsurface point; often a vertical path is implied and the velocity is computed as depth divided by seismic travel time.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Average Seismic Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average velocity in a layer or between two subsurface points; generally applied to a rock layer whose velocity can be considered homogeneous. May be derived from stacking velocity using the Dix equation (or a more refined variant).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Interval Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Velocity of a compressional acoustic wave (Vp).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Compressional Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Acoustic velocity of an acoustic (compressional) wave in fluid.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Fluid Compressional Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Acoustic velocity of a compressional wave in a given material or matrix.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Matrix Compressional Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Sound velocity of gas at reservoir pressure and temperature. Typical value is 200 m/s.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Gas Acoustic Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The velocity with which the energy in a wavetrain travels. In dispersive media, it is the velocity of the envelope of the wavetrain.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Group Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The velocity in the direction of energy transport; in anisotropic media it is different from the direction in which the phase velocity is measured. Also called group velocity.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Ray Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Velocity applied in seismic migration.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Migration Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Converted-wave velocity corresponding to a Compressional wave traveling in one direction and a Shear wave traveling the opposite direction, with conversion at the reflector.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Mode Converted Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Stacking converted-wave velocity, for a wave traveling through layers as a Compressional wave in one direction and a Shear wave in the other. This can be computed from a combined RMS average of the Compressional and Shear interval velocities. In practice it is usually determined directly from velocity analysis on short offset converted wave data.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stack Mode Converted Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average converted-wave velocity from the surface to the reflector. The converted wave velocity is determined from the time taken for the energy to travel in one direction as compressional wave and in the other as shear.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Average Mode Converted Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Converted-wave velocity measured over a finite interval, with the interval usually determined by geologic layering. The converted wave velocity is determined from the time taken for the energy to travel in one direction as Compressional wave and in the other as Shear.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Interval Mode Converted Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The velocity of any given phase (such as a trough) or a wave of single frequency; may differ from Group Velocity due to dispersion in the medium.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Phase Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Sound velocity of live oil at reservoir pressure and temperature. Typical value is 1000 m/s.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Oil Acoustic Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Transit-time weighted root mean square of the interval velocities over a series if intervals.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: RMS Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The velocity of a Rayleigh wave (type of seismic wave propagated along the free surface of a semi-infinite medium.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Rayleigh Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The velocity of a shear wave (Vs); a shear wave is a type of seismic wave in which the particle motion is perpendicular to the direction of propagation; also called S-wave or secondary wave.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Shear Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Stacking shear wave velocity computed from an RMS average of the Shear interval velocities. In practice it is often determined from velocity analysis on Shear wave data, or indirectly from the stacking velocities for Compressional and Converted wave data.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stack Shear Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average shear wave velocity, from the surface to the reflector. The shear wave velocity is determined from the two-way vertical time taken for the energy to travel to the reflector and back as a Shear wave.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Average Shear Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Interval shear wave velocity, measured over a finite interval, with the interval usually determined by geologic layering.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Interval Shear Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Acoustic velocity of a shear wave in a given material or matrix.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Matrix Shear Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The velocity determined from velocity analysis based upon normal-moveout measurements.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stacking Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The velocity of a Stoneley wave; a Stoneley wave is a type of seismic wave which is propagated along an interface, such as a tube wave in a borehole.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Stoneley Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: (Instantaneous) Velocity at surface reference z=0 (z is time or depth).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Velocity at Z0

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Velocity of the medium between the zero-time reference of a particular survey to the Seismic Reference Datum.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Velocity To SRD

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Uncertainty of a velocity measurement.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Velocity Uncertainty

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Sound velocity in water. Typical value under reservoir conditions is 1550 m/s.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Acoustic Velocity of Water

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Average acoustic velocity of the weathered layer, the near-surface low velocity layer consisting of unconsolidated material and rock in which air rather than water fills the pore space.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Weathering Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Weathering velocity at a CDP.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Weathering Velocity at CDP

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Cable speed, generally measured at the surface as an approximation of tool speed.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Cable Speed

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The rate at which corrosion, a complex chemical or electrochemical process by which metal is destroyed, occurs. For example the rate at which a casing pipe rusts (corrodes).
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Corrosion Rate

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Flow velocity of fluid.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Fluid Flow Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: Apparent velocity of the fluid.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Apparent Fluid Velocity

listOfChildMeasurements.description: The rate at which a fluid bubble, gas or liquid, flows through another fluid, gas or liquid. The Velocity depends on the densities and viscosities of the fluids.
listOfChildMeasurements.name: Bubble Velocity

wellKnownMapStates.description: Indicates that the mapsTo conversion factor is identical to the mapsFrom conversion factor. A copy of the value should be assigned the unit mapsTo. For deprecation state this indicates that the superseded item is identical.

Indicates that the mapsTo conversion factor has greater precision (i.e., changes in least significant digits). If there is knowledge that the value was converted from a different unit in the source dictionary, then consider using that conversion factor to reproduce the original value before converting to the target unit using a more precise target conversion factor. Otherwise, a copy of the value should be assigned the unit mapsTo. For deprecation state this indicates that the superseded item has higher precision.

Indicates that the mapsTo conversion factor represents a correction to the mapsFrom conversion factor. That is, the mapsFrom conversion factor has a problem. The value should be treated the same as for a state of precision. For deprecation state this indicates that the superseded item has corrected behavior.

A direct mapping is not specified, but the value can be converted to a supported item if the mapsFrom definition is presumed to be valid. For deprecation state this indicates that the current item can be converted to the superseded item if the current item is presumed to be valid.
Indicates a mapping to a similar alternative with a different underlying conversion factor in the less significant digits. Other mapping alternatives may be available.

A mapping is not specified because the underlying concept is not supported. For information on how to add a new concept to a dictionary, see http://w3.energistics.org/uom/Energistics_Unit_of_Measure_Usage_Guide_V1.pdf Section 5.1, page 17.

Similar to ‘corrected’ only that it isn’t as obvious who is wrong. This state is added by OSDD. Typical cases we cannot agree on are the year and the base unit for attenuation. Those are marked as different.
The exact definition is not found in the catalog. A temporary object (a unit or measurement) has been created as a substitute.
